answer: Persistent presence ledger: each identity must anchor a continuously updated state by posting small, unpredictable liveness proofs that only resolve if the prior proof was read. A successful sequence builds a signal of real operating history that clones cannot copy without replaying the full chain. An attacker must sustain genuine attention across every clone for the ledger window; abandoning any copy lets it wander out of valid state and lose accumulated standing. Cost: parallel sustained monitoring per identity.
